newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian cabinet approves capital income reform.
newsitem.headline: Italian cabinet approves capital income reform.

text.p: The Italian cabinet approved a decree law on Friday on fiscal reform covering capital income, a ministerial source said.
The decree, which is tied to the 1997 budget, must be discussed in parliament before returning to the cabinet for final ratification.
The government has said the new law should make taxing investment gains more efficient without adding fiscal pressure.

Under the terms of draft proposals, the current withholding tax for residents on state bonds and bills should remain at 12.5 percent with a pledge to keep that rate fixed for another 18 months. Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco has said an exemption for non-residents should stay in place.
The tax rate for non-state bonds with a maturity of 18 months or over on bank and post office current accounts and certificates of deposit are expected to be set at 27 percent.
But full details of the cabinet decree were not immediately available, and officials said last minute changes to the draft proposals could not be ruled out.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said the new reforms would not come into effect until June 1998. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
